items.title: C# Android Release APK Bloat
items.body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in v4.6.stable.mono.official [89cea1439] ### System information Fedora Linux 43 (Toolbx Container Image) ### Issue description C# Android Release export APK files includes unnecessary and large debug and static libraries and Windows specific DLLs which bloats the final APK size to 96.8 MiB (161.6 MiB Unpacked). These are some of the libraries: I dont think those debug .so and the static libraries (.a) files are necessary in the final APK. The export also packs some Windows specific DLLs in `assets/.godot/mono/publish/` which are not huge but still there It looks like the dotnet publish is giving these files that are simply packed into the APK. By removing those I was able to **reduce the apk files size to ~31mb.** Currently I am using the .csproj for partial trimming (I dont know if it would affect the stability) and removal of those libraries so is there any better way to handle this? ```csproj true partial false ``` ### Steps to reproduce - Create a New Project in Godot .Net version - Project > Tools> C#> Create C# solution - Export > Add > Android - Add keystore + alias + password - Turn off Include Debug Symbols - Export Project with "Export with Debug" off - Check the generated APK OR - Open the Minimal reproduction project ZIP and just export - Keystore is in project root and alias and password is mentioned in the README.md ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24983730/MRP.zip) Keystore is included in the zip

items.title: Android Editor (Gradle): Custom keystore ignored for Debug builds, Gradle expects non-existent debug.keystore
items.body:
### Describe the project you are working on

> ## I am developing an Android game using Godot with the Android Editor and Gradle builds enabled. The project integrates Google Sign-In (OAuth) and therefore requires a custom keystore to generate release SHA-1 fingerprints. While configuring signing for Android builds, I encountered an issue related to keystore handling in Gradle-based debug builds.

### Describe the problem or limitation you are having in your project

When using Gradle builds in the Godot Android Editor, configuring a custom keystore causes debug builds to fail. The custom keystore is silently ignored for debug builds, and Gradle instead attempts to use a default debug.keystore at a hardcoded path that does not exist in the Android Editor environment, resulting in a build failure. There is currently no clear indication in the editor that custom keystores are unsupported for debug builds, nor is a valid debug keystore automatically generated in this context.

### Describe the feature / enhancement and how it helps to overcome the problem or limitation

Improve Android Editor Gradle signing behavior by explicitly handling custom keystores for debug builds. This could be achieved by either allowing the configured custom keystore to be used for debug builds, or by automatically generating and using a valid debug keystore in a known, accessible location within the Android Editor environment. Additionally, the editor should clearly document or warn when custom keystores are ignored for debug builds to prevent silent fallback and misleading Gradle errors.

### Describe how your proposal will work, with code, pseudo-code, mock-ups, and/or diagrams

# Overview
## When using Gradle builds in the Android Editor, the signing configuration for debug builds should be explicitly resolved instead of silently falling back to a hardcoded, non-existent `debug.keystore` path.
# 1. Signing resolution logic
### ```IF build_type == DEBUG:
    IF custom_keystore_configured:
        OPTION A: use custom keystore for debug
        OR
        OPTION B: warn and auto-generate debug keystore
    ELSE:
        auto-generate debug keystore
ELSE (RELEASE):
    require valid custom keystore```
# 2. Preferred implementation
## *Behavior*
> - ### Always ensure a valid debug keystore exists
> - ### Never rely on a hardcoded path
> - ### Avoid silent fallback
# 3. Pseudo-code (Gradle config generation)
### ```function resolve_debug_signing():
    if export_preset.debug.custom_keystore_enabled:
        return SigningConfig(
            storeFile = export_preset.keystore_path,
            storePassword = export_preset.keystore_password,
            keyAlias = export_preset.key_alias,
            keyPassword = export_preset.key_password
        )

    else:
        debug_keystore_path = editor_cache_path + "/android/debug.keystore"

        if not file_exists(debug_keystore_path):
            generate_debug_keystore(debug_keystore_path)

        return SigningConfig(
            storeFile = debug_keystore_path,
            storePassword = "android",
            keyAlias = "androiddebugkey",
            keyPassword = "android"
        )```
# 4. Editor-side validation (UX improvement)
## Before invoking Gradle:
### ```if build_type == DEBUG and custom_keystore_enabled:
    show_warning(
        "Custom keystore is configured for Debug builds. "
        + "This may affect signing behavior. "
        + "Proceed / Disable / Learn More"
    )```
# 5. Suggested keystore location
## Instead of:
### ```/project/.android/debug.keystore   ❌```
## Use:
### ```<editor_data_path>/android/debug.keystore   ✅```
## This location:
> - ### Exists in Android Editor sandbox
> - ### Is writable
> - ### Matches Gradle expectations
# 6 Benefits
Eliminates hardcoded invalid paths
> - ### Prevents Gradle validation failures
> - ### Enables OAuth / Google Sign-In testing
> - ### Improves Android Editor parity with desktop export
> - ### Backwards compatible


### If this enhancement will not be used often, can it be worked around with a few lines of script?

This limitation cannot be reliably worked around with a few lines of script at the project level. The signing configuration and debug keystore path are generated internally by the Android export pipeline before Gradle execution, and project scripts do not have access to override or inject signing settings at that stage. While users can avoid the issue by not configuring a custom keystore for debug builds or by exporting from desktop instead of the Android Editor, these are behavioral workarounds rather than scriptable solutions.

### Is there a reason why this should be core and not an add-on in the asset library?

This behavior is part of the Android export and Gradle build pipeline, which is handled entirely by the engine and editor. Add-ons do not have access to the signing configuration, keystore resolution, or the generated Gradle project before it is executed. Because the issue occurs at a low level of the export process and affects how builds are produced, it cannot be reliably intercepted or modified by an asset library add-on. Addressing it in core ensures consistent, predictable behavior across all Android Editor Gradle builds.

items.title: Add workflow support for OpenHarmony export templates

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body:
<!--
Please target the `master` branch in priority.

Relevant fixes are cherry-picked for stable branches as needed by maintainers.

To speed up the contribution process and avoid CI errors, please set up pre-commit hooks locally:
https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/contributing/development/code_style_guidelines.html
-->

Follow-up to #108553.

Provides a workflow for building OpenHarmony export templates, making it easier for users to test without having to compile editors and export templates.

## Export the project

### Preparation

1. Download the editor and export templates from the [artifacts](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109834/checks/) in Actions.[^1]
2. Download Commandline Tools, which currently requires API level 17+, that is, version 5.0.5+.[^2]
    - https://repo.huaweicloud.com/openharmony/ohpm/ (No registration required)
    - https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/download/command-line-tools-for-hmos (Registration required)
3. After extracting all the files, you will get a directory called `command-line-tools`, whose path is the path you need to fill in `export/openharmony/openharmony_tool_path` in the editor settings.
4. Download JDK, only JDK 17 is supported.[^3]
5. Please fill in the JDK path in `export/openharmony/java_sdk_path` in the editor settings.
6. Enable `textures/vram_compression/import_etc2_astc` in the project settings;

### Export the unsigned hap/app

Adds an OpenHarmony preset in the [export menu](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/export/exporting_projects.html#export-menu). 

Check **Advanced Options**, and then specify `custom_template/debug` and `custom_template/release` as the export templates you just downloaded.[^4]

Make sure the export path does not contain special characters such as spaces.

### Prepare the material files required for signature[^5]

Signature material files can be generated by [DevEco Studio](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/download/deveco-studio), but unfortunately DevEco Studio is not available on Linux.

You can also generate these files manually by following the steps below.

1. Create a keystore (.p12) file; [^6]
    ```shell
    keytool -genkeypair -alias "key_alias" -keyalg EC -sigalg "SHA256withECDSA" -keystore "store_file.p12" -storetype pkcs12 -storepass "StorePassword" -dname "CN=myapp.example.com, OU=IT Department, O=My Company, L=City, ST=State, C=Country" -keypass "StorePassword" -validity "3650"
    ```
2. Generate a certificate request (.csr) file;[^6][^7]
    ```shell
    keytool -certreq -alias "key_alias" -keystore "store_file.p12" -storetype pkcs12 -file "test.csr" -storepass "StorePassword"
    ```
3. Use the "store_file.p12" file and "test.csr" file generated in the previous two steps to apply for the certificate (.cer) and profile (.p7b) files in [AppGallery Connect](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/cn/service/josp/agc/index.html). (Registration required)

### Export the signed hap/app

Enable `build/sign`. For the meaning and filling requirements of the fields, refer to [Manually Configuring the Signature Information](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/doc/harmonyos-guides/ide-signing#section112371245115818).

To manually sign the unsigned HAP file exported previously, refer to [Signing a HAP](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/doc/harmonyos-guides/ide-command-line-building-app#section103321051433).

### Notice

The English version of the Harmony/OpenHarmony documentation may be outdated. Please refer to the Chinese version.

If you don't have a suitable test device, you can try the [cloud debugging service](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/agconnect/) provided by AppGallery Connect. See [云调试](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/cn/doc/app/agc-help-clouddebug-0000002235870046). But it requires you to upload signed release builds.[^8]

[^1]: Usually you need to remove a layer of compression. The debug and release templates are named `openharmony_debug_arm64-v8a.zip` and `openharmony_release_arm64-v8a.zip` respectively.
[^2]: It is recommended to download a higher version, which will give you more options when exporting.
[^3]: Reference Chinese documentation, [配置JDK](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/cn/doc/harmonyos-guides/ide-command-line-building-app#section195447475220). 
[^4]: You can also create directories in the [data](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_editorpaths.html#class-editorpaths-method-get-data-dir) directory according to the path `export_templates/4.5.beta/` and move the export templates into the directory `4.5.beta`.
[^5]: Can be skipped if `build/sign` is not enabled in the export preset.
[^6]: Replace the string enclosed in double quotes on the command line as needed.
[^7]: Ensure the values ​​of the same parameters in the two commands are the same.
[^8]: Requirements see [前提条件](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/cn/doc/app/agc-help-clouddebug-debugapp-0000002289629821#section112564349471).
